I start with the question of whether you need to use Emacs to think like an Emacs user. item.title: Clutch: Query, Browse and Edit Databases Without Leaving Emacs
item.description:
youtube

Clutch is an Emacs package for querying and browsing databases, and for staging SQL row edits with a preview before anything runs. Results open in an interactive grid, and nothing is written until you review the exact SQL and confirm. Supported databases: MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MongoDB and Redis natively, plus Oracle, SQL Server, ClickHouse, DuckDB and other databases through JDBC. In this demo we use PostgreSQL over its native protocol, then DuckDB over JDBC. Chapters 0:00 Connect and run a query 0:23 Foreign keys and NULL faces 0:32 Per-column displayers 0:57 Rectangle select and Refine 1:22 Aggregate and server-side filter 1:38 Stage, preview and submit an edit 1:59 Long JSON hover preview 2:35 Insert and delete rows 3:15 JDBC databases (DuckDB) What you will see - Run SQL in a normal buffer with C-c C-c - Foreign keys are underlined; NULL has its own face - Per-column displayers: turn raw values into colored labels - Rectangle selection (C-x SPC), then Refine (-r) to exclude rows and columns before copying as TSV, CSV or an Org table - Aggregate selected numeric cells, and filter with a server-side WHERE - Stage edits, preview the exact SQL (C-c C-p), then confirm - Long JSON hover preview (off by default: set clutch-cell-preview-style to child-frame) - Insert and delete rows through a form - JDBC: a Java 17+ agent runs beside Emacs; the same UI works over JDBC Install M-x package-install RET clutch Requirements: Emacs 29.1+. SQLite needs nothing else. Other native backends need their own Emacs package, and JDBC needs Java 17+. GitHub: https://github.com/LuciusChen/clutch MELPA: https://melpa.org/#/clutch ,#Emacs #SQL #Database

item.title: ¿Por qué Doom Emacs es el secreto de los expertos?
item.description:
youtube

¿Sientes que Emacs es demasiado complejo pero quieres aprovechar todo su poder? En este video te revelo el secreto mejor guardado para dominar este editor: Doom Emacs. Doom Emacs no es solo una skin, es un framework "supervitaminado" con más de 150 módulos que transforma por completo tu flujo de trabajo en Linux. Te guiaré paso a paso en la instalación y configuración sobre Ubuntu 26.04 y Pop!_OS, para que pases de principiante a experto sin complicaciones. En este tutorial aprenderás: ✅ Qué es Doom Emacs y por qué NO es un fork. ✅ Requisitos previos: Instalación de dependencias (Git, Ripgrep, fd-find). ✅ Cómo instalar fuentes con glifos (JetBrains Mono y Nerd Fonts). ✅ Configuración de archivos clave: init.el, config.el y packages.el. ✅ Sincronización de módulos y optimización de la interfaz. ✅ Trucos para integrar Doom Emacs directamente en tu escritorio (archivos .desktop). Si eres usuario de Vim o NeoVim y buscas una alternativa potente con modo Evil, este video es para ti. ¡No dejes que la fama de "difícil" te detenga y dale una oportunidad al editor definitivo! This is a video about how I migrated my Obsidian Vault to Org Mode, converting markdown to org using a combination of justfile recipes, bash scripts, DuckDB SQL queries, and Pandoc Lua filters. 📺 Watch the full Emacs Everywhere series here ► https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLLHUnpt36CJg In this series, I share my Emacs workflow, including all the bits that are not directly about Emacs: ► In part 1, I introduce the basics of Doom Emacs, teaching you how to learn Emacs. ► In part 2, I show how I migrated from Obsidian Vault to Org Mode, using pandoc to convert markdown to org, and pandoc-lua to restructure my org notes in a way that fits my new org based workflow. ► In part 3, I go through all the major features of Org Mode, covering a few packages I find useful. ► In part 4, I describe the incremental backup strategy that I use to ensure I never lose any of my org notes. 🔗 Resources: 💻 GitHub repo: https://github.com/DataLabTechTV/md2org/ 📝 Blog post: https://datalabtechtv.com/posts/emacs-everywhere-part-2-migrating-from-obsidian-to-org-mode/ 📚 Org Mode: https://orgmode.org/org.html 📚 Lua: https://www.luadocs.com/ 📚 Pandoc Lua: https://pandoc.org/lua-filters.html 📚 DuckDB: https://duckdb.org/docs/lts/sql/statements/overview 🔔 Subscribe for more deep dives data science, data engineering, and all things data! ☁️ Follow the channel on Bluesky: https://bsky.app/profile/datalabtechtv.com 🎧 Join our community's Discord: https://discord.gg/6xpe827ANZ 👽 Join our subreddit: https://www.reddit.com/r/DataLabTechTV/ 💻 Check out the channel's GitHub: https://github.com/DataLabTechTV 🌐 Visit our website for blog posts: https://datalabtechtv.com ​#emacs #orgmode #justfile #bash #shellscripting #duckdb #pandoc #lua 0:00 Intro 6:08 md2org: Project Structure and Configuration 25:39 m2org: Just, Bash, DuckDB, and Pandoc Lua 1:07:46 Outro
